microstructure: Short-horizon price changes are driven more directly by order-flow imbalance relative to available depth than by trade volume alone.
Queue and depth imbalance contain directional information, while deeper book shape and resiliency matter beyond the top level.
Short-run reversals can compensate liquidity provision, but unexpected shocks can withdraw passive liquidity and create price-discovery gaps.
project_failure_lessons: A rolling auction center contaminated by the excursion can report artificial mean reversion.
A small move toward value is not a completed rejection.
Forcing every excursion into a reversal ignores accepted price discovery.
The source dealing range, its boundary, the excursion and the classification window must be frozen and stateful.

first_week_selection.method: Python random.Random(seed).choice over chronologically sorted eligible UTC Mondays

rejection_branch.definition: completed close at least 0.25 ATR back inside the frozen boundary before two accepted outside closes

acceptance_branch.definition: two consecutive completed closes outside the frozen boundary
acceptance_branch.invalidation: 0.15 ATR back inside the frozen boundary

execution.decision_data: completed five-minute bars and previously observed features only
execution.entry: next executable one-minute NautilusTrader bar after decision

promotion.rule: Only a passing first-week NautilusTrader result may reveal a second week.
